title: Savings vs Latency Sparkline Configurator for Batch+Cache
creator: Ava Ramirez
description: Goal: Ship a compact configurator in the Redwood Console that helps operators tune batching and prefix/KV cache parameters by visualizing trade-offs between token cost savings and p95 latency. The UI combines a sparkline overview, suggested policy presets, and inline explainers/guardrails to reduce risk when enabling aggressive aggregation or long TTLs. This ticket covers prototype screens, copy iterations, accessibility pass, and handoff artifacts for engineering.
objectives: Surface immediate cost vs latency trade-off in a single-line sparkline that updates live with simulated traffic presets
Provide three contextual suggestions (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) with one-click apply and short explainers
Expose safety guardrails and a rollback CTA when suggested settings increase tail latency beyond baseline SLA
Include microcopy and a11y annotations so SREs can enable features in high-regulated tenants with confidence
acceptance_criteria: Sparkline component demonstrates median cost change + p95 latency delta when switching presets
Prototype contains tooltip-level explainers for each config knob: batch window, max batch size, KV TTL, prefix prefetch size
Design tokens and sizes match console theme; color-blind safe palette approved by accessibility review
Developer handoff includes component states, animations, and data contract examples for simulated preview API
Product sign-off obtained and PM added rollout schedule to console-2025.03 release notes
usability_findings: Moderated testing (n=6) showed users interpret the sparkline as 'cost forecast' but initially missed the p95 latency marker — moved marker to use a bolder contrasting stroke
Participants wanted a short example of 'how this breaks' — added a concise failure-mode callout describing increased throughput risk with long TTLs
One user asked for a CSV export of simulated runs for audit — added as an engineering wishlist item
design_decisions: Use a single compact sparkline + two-value delta (cost % / p95 ms) to keep the panel lightweight in route-level pages
Presets are contextualized by workload templates (chat, embeddings, rerank) rather than absolute token counts
Guardrail threshold is set to 1.2x baseline p95 by default; editable via advanced settings for Dedicated customers
tradeoffs: Showing more than three presets increased cognitive load during tests; limited to three with an 'advanced' modal
Real-time simulation of live traffic is expensive — we surface quick approximations and an 'accurate simulation' async job for heavier audits
Aggressive presets provide better cost wins but require stronger rollout tooling; tied rollout step to canary with automatic rollback
accessibility_notes: Color choices verified against WCAG AA for contrast; sparklines include accessible text alternatives
Keyboard-only controls are required for preset selection and 'apply' action; added visible focus states
All explainers and failure modes must be available as expandable regions rather than hover-only tooltips
copy_iterations: v1 microcopy used 'Savings' / 'Latency' labels — testers preferred 'Estimated token savings' and 'p95 latency delta'
Short guardrail copy added: 'Rollback automatically if latency increases more than {{threshold}}'
CTA changed from 'Enable' to 'Apply and Stage Canary' to reinforce rollout behavior
engineering_notes: Need an endpoint for simulated preview: POST /console/v1/simulate-batchcache with workload template and knobs
Frontend should accept a minimal contract: {preset_id, cost_delta_pct, p95_delta_ms, confidence_interval} — see proto in handoff doc
Backend will queue accurate-sim jobs and surface async job links in the panel; quota gating required for hosted tenants
